newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ dollar closes higher but hits resistance.
newsitem.headline: NZ dollar closes higher but hits resistance.

text.p: The New Zealand dollar closed higher on Tuesday but ran into firm resistance at US$0.6910, dealers said.
The currency closed at 0.6903/10 after trading a 0.6886-6909 range. On the Trade-Weighted Index it firmed to 65.52 from 65.38.

Dealers said there was an underlying bid tone, with some good Asian interest. A TV3 opinion poll on Monday showed a slight firming in support for the governing National Party, counteracting a TV1 poll at the weekend in which National slipped four points.

In the run-up to the October 12 general election, they said political concerns were balanced against demand for Kiwi linked to Eurobonds and samurais. A NZ$150 million Eurobond on behalf of Swedish Export Credit Corp was launched overnight.

Dealers said they expected a range of US$0.6880-6920 in the next few days, with quiet trade expected in the run up to two major set-pieces next week. Treasury releases its pre-election economic and fiscal update on September 12, with the Reserve Bank's economic forecasts due the following day.
